provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 258-259; antecedent 1862 text-layer lines 25072-25076; 1922 Mame printed p. 134, artifact PDF p. 248
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 5 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: presta quesumus omnipotens -> ftesta quasumus omnipo tens; obseruationes -> obseruatio nes; annua -> dnnua; recolentes -> recotentes; placeamus -> place mus; 1922 Mame text layer damages 1 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): presta quesumus omnipotens -> om p nipotens; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 134, artifact PDF p. 248; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 60271 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Feria II post dominicam IV in Quadragesima) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Oratio the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.
